newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Lend Lease sees 40 pct sales rises.
newsitem.headline: Lend Lease sees 40 pct sales rises.

text.p: Property and financial services group Lend Lease Corp forecast on Sunday its project management and funds management units would post 40 percent higher revenues in the current year to June 30, 1998.

"You'll see our sales in our project management business this year up by 40 percent on last year and indications are that the following year is going to be equally strong," Lend Lease Chief Executive David Higgins told the Nine Network's Business Sunday television programme.
Lend Lease manages and funds property development projects. He said Lend Lease's funds managers expected a similar sized revenue rise of "around a 40 percent increase".
Higgins said the Australian economy appeared to be a two-tier economy and that some of Lend Lease's businesses were performing very strongly while others were weaker.
The retailing sector, which Lend Lease is exposed to through its retail property investments, had been slower but was improving, he said.
Some states and cities were also weaker than others.
Sydney had been the best market for Lend Lease, he said.
Lend Lease reported on Thursday a 15 percent rise in net profit for 1996/97 to A$322 million and forecast higher net profits and dividends for 1997/98.
